Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: Marketplace usually wins for pilot speed; direct contract wins for long-term billing flexibility and reserved capacity commitments. Below is a concise trade-off guide and proposed next steps. I attached a short pricing comparison and our marketplace quickstart PDF for procurement.

Trade-offs (summary):
- Speed: AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace onboarding + private offer = fastest (often days to a couple weeks). Direct MSA + PO can take multiple weeks to months depending on vendor legal review.
- Invoicing & PO cadence: Marketplaces typically issue monthly consolidated invoices on their billing cadence. Direct contracts allow Redwood to invoice monthly or quarterly per your PO terms and support net-30/60 terms (if pre-negotiated).
- Co-sell credits: For marketplace purchases, co-sell crediting can lag (marketplace payout schedules and attribution windows). A private offer with co-sell tagging (and coordinated partner registration) can preserve co-sell eligibility. Direct deals with an explicit co-sell clause and SOW make crediting and revenue share clearer and often faster to recognize in sales ops.
- Support & SLAs: Functional parity exists (we operate the same service), but enterprise direct agreements can include explicit SLA credits, custom support tiers, and priority routing. Marketplace purchases default to platform support levels unless we add a support augmentation via a private offer.
- Legal blockers: Common marketplace blockers are non-standard MSA exceptions, data processing terms (DPA/BAA for healthcare), and indemnity/certifications. For healthcare workloads, we can offer a DPA/BAA on a private offer — that usually solves the main procurement hurdle without a full MSA negotiation.

Recommended path for Atlas Health pilot:
1) Start with a marketplace private offer (AWS or GCP private listing) to accelerate procurement and preserve a clean invoice trail for your finance team.
2) Add a DPA/BAA as part of the private offer if you need HIPAA assurances (we can attach this to the offer).
3) Parallel track direct MSA/Reserved Capacity conversations if you expect >$X/month in steady-state usage (we can define thresholds). After 3–6 months, migrate to a reserved capacity contract to reduce per-token cost and gain billing flexibility.

Diego — quick answers from channel/co-sell POV:
- Private offer + partner registration: best balance for speed + co-sell. If Atlas accepts a private offer, we should register the opportunity in the partner portal (this protects co-sell credit). Registration upfront is recommended but not strictly required to start the pilot.
- Expected credit timing: attribution typically shows in our channel ops 1–2 reporting cycles after invoice recognition (depends on marketplace payout cadence). Expect 30–60 day lag before co-sell appears in revenue ops reporting.
- Paperwork: if they need a BAA/DPA for healthcare, add it to the private offer. That avoids modifying our standard MSA during the pilot.

Laura — for billing: can we confirm if our marketplace invoice can include a PO reference line (so their AP can process it) and if we can support net-30 on a direct invoice if they insist on a direct PO? If there's a restriction, call it out and we can propose an internal workaround (e.g., Redwood issues monthly invoice but marketplace payment handles charges).

If both agree: recommend we open a private offer for the pilot, attach DPA, and include a small pilot SKU with explicit renewal terms so transition to reserved capacity is straightforward.

Thanks — K
